WHERE THE TWO JOURNEY WIDGETS LAND IN HUDDLE

Static placement mockups, not clickable prototypes — the question is where these things end up.

Everything is lifted from the real app: tokens from src/styles.css, rail geometry from Rail.tsx (56px, bg-primary, 40px items, 18px icons @1.8 stroke), view registry from HuddleApp.tsx:380. journey's raw colours map onto Huddle tokens — purple send arrow = --ai, green start/complete = --success, orange pause = --warning, cream band = oklch(0.975 0.032 92).

Dashed purple outline = added by this work.

ARTBOARD 1 — docked in the chat column

Both widgets sit in a two-up grid under a 'Docked in this huddle' strip, ABOVE the transcript, inside Iris's 1:1 only. They are pinned furniture, not chat messages — so they don't scroll away like the checklist widget does, and Iris can reference them in her reply.

The context panel and huddle list are untouched.

PRE-EXISTING BUG THIS WORK HAS TO STEP AROUND

Rail.tsx already offers four entries but HuddleApp.tsx:380 renders only three views. Line 39 marks Memory active when view === 'huddle', and line 45 maps Memory to 'huddle' — so clicking Memory silently renders Huddles. It is decorative today.

Adding two more views to that three-way ternary compounds it. The prototype assumes the registry becomes a VIEW MAP keyed by id, which fixes Memory in the same change rather than leaving a fourth broken entry beside two new working ones.

NOT A SECOND BOARD

Both views read the SAME tasks.journey_tasks mirror the Board reads — one read model, three surfaces. The topic tree is the only thing Huddle does not already hold; it comes from journey through a proxy tool (Lane A).

Every control writes through the existing update_task: ▶ = UP_NEXT→DOING (still behind the confirm-intent gate), ✓ = the user's own DONE, ⏸ = park with the parking-lot tag, ▲/✓ Today = move_task_to_day / unschedule_task. No new writer to the mirror; it re-syncs in ~1–3s.

PHONE

Two-up doesn't fit 390px, so the widgets stack and the second collapses to a one-line summary that expands on tap.

The mobile switcher in HuddleApp is currently a 3-entry row of labels. Six entries means icon-over-label; the two new ones are dashed here. This is the switcher's real constraint, not a redesign of it.
